Subject: Re: Production: Checkout 5xx/429 spike

Quick triage notes (first 20m):
- Root signal: sudden request fanout due to customer-side retries + increased per-request latency (median p95 token latency rose from 60ms -> 210ms for the checkout models).
- Autoscaler: borderline saturated. There were 2 allocation failures in the region (GPU pool out of ephemeral slots) at 09:01 and 09:09; autoscaler attempted but hit soft limits.
- Throttling: internal rate limiter began returning 429s once per-tenant burst thresholds were hit.

Immediate mitigations applied (09:30):
- Scaled dedicated checkout pool by +30% (manual reserve of spare nodes).
- Temporarily routed non-critical traffic to a lower-capacity model variant and enabled prefix caching on the checkout route.
- Raised retry-window guidance to customer (ask them to backoff to 5s).

Observations: retry amplification looks likely — a small fraction of long-tail requests triggers client-side retries that multiply load across the pool. We will keep the scaled nodes until traffic stabilizes.

I created a short Grafana dashboard (link below). I also saved the raw traces from FinCo to S3 for deeper analysis.

Evelyn
SRE Manager, Redwood Inference

Subject: Post-incident summary and next steps — FinCo checkout impact (5xx/429 spike)

Linda — thank you again for the quick report and traces. Below is a concise post-incident summary and our committed follow-ups. Please review and flag anything you want prioritized.

Incident summary:
- Window: 2027-07-11 08:45 — 2027-07-11 11:10 PST (primary spike), secondary fluctuations through 07/12 as customers retried.
- Impact: elevated 5xx (~6%) and 429 (~12%) on the /v1/checkout/generate route for FinCo customers during the peak promotion window. Some clients observed checkout timeouts and increased latency.
- Primary contributing factors: client-side retry amplification + autoscaler soft limits + p95 token latency increase due to suboptimal kernel selection under that traffic mix.

Immediate mitigations applied by Redwood:
- Manual scale of checkout pool (+30%) and hold of scaled capacity until 07/13.
- Temporary routing to a lower-throughput fallback model for non-critical flows.
- Enabled prefix/KV caching and adjusted rate-limiter thresholds for FinCo tenant to reduce 429s while maintaining fair-share.

Action items (owner — ETA):
- Runtime engineering (Jonas) — Investigate kernel selection path and reproduce p95 regression. Possible rollback or targeted canary. (ETA: 2027-07-15)
- SRE (Evelyn) — Add an alert for 'retry amplification detection' (pattern: rising client-side retry rate concurrent with p95 increase + autoscaler saturation). Build a runbook entry for manual scale/diversion. (ETA: 2027-07-14)
- Product/CS (Marcus/Stephanie) — Propose a short-term SLO concession for FinCo's promotion window and coordinate credits if needed. Draft communication for FinCo execs. (ETA: 2027-07-13)
- Capacity planning (Marcus/Jonas) — Review checkout pool reservation policy and recommend minimum spare capacity for high-traffic tenants. (ETA: 2027-07-20)
- Engineering (Jonas) — Add a targeted microbenchmark harness for the checkout model mix to detect kernel regressions in CI. (ETA: 2027-07-22)

Follow-ups and transparency:
- We will share a formal postmortem doc (internal + sanitized external) by 2027-07-16.
- I uploaded initial traces and draft notes to the shared Drive (link below).
- We will schedule a post-incident review with FinCo SREs and product on 2027-07-14 10:00 PST.
